name: Optical transceivers (800G / 1.6T)
thesis: The interconnect that wires GPU clusters together — roughly six per GPU. 800G is running well below demand, and Nvidia spent $4B locking up the laser supply.

gauge.rationale: Nvidia's $4B EML laser lock-up pushed rivals' supply past 2027 as 800G demand ran 40–60% ahead of capacity.

why_it_gates: AI training clusters need roughly six high-speed transceivers per GPU to sustain bandwidth across the fabric — far more than conventional servers. The binding chokepoint is the 200G-per-lane EML laser chip, made by only a handful of firms, so optics quietly gate how large a usable GPU cluster can actually be wired together.

catalysts.text: 1.6T modules ramp past ~5M units; 800G coherent becomes the AI-network standard
Nvidia CPO (Quantum-X / Spectrum-X Photonics) begins displacing pluggables at scale-out

what_loosens_it: EML capacity expansions (Coherent, Lumentum, ELASER), silicon-photonics substitution, and the shift to co-packaged optics. But McKinsey sees 800G short through 2027 and 1.6T through 2029.

developments.text: McKinsey: 800G production 40–60% below demand through 2027; 1.6T shortfall 30–40% through 2029
AI optical transceiver market seen ~$26B in 2026; component shortages flagged as the key capacity bottleneck
Nvidia invests $4B across Coherent and Lumentum to secure EML / CPO capacity
